title: The Importance of Retelling Stories of Success
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This post says leaders who focus on pushing forward often forget to remind the team of what it has already achieved, and that retelling success stories is work only leaders can do. It builds on the common view that great leaders are storytellers but takes a step further, asking them to repeat stories of adversity overcome, collaboration, and the origins of good ideas at every opportunity. The author gives a rationale from memory: because memories are stored in story-like structures, retelling preserves the details of how success happened. That makes the stories a recipe for future success rather than mere good feeling. The result is renewed confidence and motivation to repeat the success.
points: Beyond celebrating wins, leaders should keep reliving past team successes through repeated stories.
The post separates ordinary persuasive storytelling from the deliberate retelling of success stories.
The suggested story types include overcoming adversity, individual passion, collaboration, and how a great idea originated and came to fruition.
Retelling works because it preserves the details that act as a recipe for repeating success.
quotes: Revisiting the many accomplishments of the team is essential work only leaders can perform. Beyond celebrating short-term successes, every team needs to relive the many great outcomes they have produced. Good leaders promote the weight of this success through the stories they tell and retell.

But the best leaders take storytelling one step further. They tell and retell stories of success, accomplishment, and excellence every chance they get. They look for opportunities, venues, and forums to share the stories of team success.

Good leaders tell stories of overcoming adversity or challenge, stories about the passion of a specific team member to push ahead, stories about the power of collaboration, stories regarding the origin of a great idea, stories about how a great idea came to fruition. They emphasize what people should remember and work hard to replicate.

In fact, reminding the team of the many successes they contributed to in the not-so-distant past is about much more than promoting positive feelings. It recounts the recipe for future team success. Because memories are stored in the brain in story-like structures, the retelling of success stories gives people the details they need to preserve a powerful recollection.

With a renewed memory of success, team members are motivated to recapture the feelings and confidence that only success can generate. Everyone loves a good story, but they relish the success stories they were a part of. Good leaders remind the team of what they have accomplished so they are motivated to repeat that success.
